THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY ASHOK S. KINAGI J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
JUDGMENT
These two appeals arising out of the judgment and award dated 10.04.2019 passed in MVC No.477/2017 by the I Addl. District and Sessions Judge, Raichur.

sentences.text: 2. Parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.
The petitioner has filed the appeal in MFA No.201309/2019 seeking enhancement of compensation and respondent-Corporation filed the appeal in MFA No.201227/2019, challenging the quantum.

3. Facts giving rise to filing of these appeals are as under:
On 14.02.2017, the petitioner boarded a bus from Raichur towards Sirwar bearing registration No.KA-36/F- 1047 and the driver of the said bus driven the same in a rash and negligent manner in a high speed and lost control over it and turtle by the side of the road by causing accident.
Due the said impact, the petitioner sustained NC: 2024:KHC-K:3862-DB injuries.
It is contended that the petitioner is working as a Lecturer in Government Pre-University College, Sirwar.
It is contended that the petitioner has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the claim petition claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in the accident.
4. The respondent filed the written statement in which the averments made in the claim petition were denied and prays to dismiss the claim petition.
5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.

6. In order to prove the case, the petitioner examined herself as PW.1 and examined the Principal of Pre-University College, Sirwar, as PW.2 so also examined two doctors as PWs.3 and 4 and got marked 179 documents as Exs.P1 to P179.
On behalf of the respondent, driver of the bus examined as RW.1 and Security Officer was examined as RW.2 and got marked documents as Exs.R1 to R7.

The Tribunal, after hearing NC: 2024:KHC-K:3862-DB both sides and on the assessment of oral and documentary evidence allowed the petition in part with costs and it is ordered that the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.14,27,192/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization of the award amount.
The respondent is directed to deposited the compensation amount with interest within a period one month from the date of award.

7. Being dissatisfied with the compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner has filed appeal in MFA No.201309/2019 seeking enhancement of compensation and respondent-Corporation has Jyoti W/O Rajshekar vs The Divisional Coantroller on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139526231/
3 filed appeal in MFA No.201227/2019 challenging the quantum.
8.

sentences.text: Heard, learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for the respondent-Corporation.
9. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that, the petitioner has not claimed medical expenses from the Government.
He submits that PW.2 has clearly stated in his examination in chief that the petitioner has not NC: 2024:KHC-K:3862-DB claimed any medical expenditure from the Government.

He submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in recoding the finding that the petitioner is a Government Servant and if there is any disability in she can claim medical expenditure by producing medical bills in the office Accounts Branch.
He submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in not granting compensation under the head of medical expenses.

Hence,
on these grounds he prays to allow the appeal filed by the petitioner and prays to dismiss the appeal filed by the respondent-Corporation.

10. Per contra, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent/Corporation submits that admittedly the petitioner is working as a Lecturer in Government Pre- University College, Sirwar,
even after the accident she continued in service.
Hence, she is not entitled for loss of future earning capacity.
He submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in granting compensation under the head loss of future earning.
He submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in granting compensation under NC: 2024:KHC-K:3862-DB the head loss of future income.
Hence, on these grounds prays to allow the appeal filed by the respondent- Corporation and dismiss the appeal filed by the petitioner.
11. Perused the records and considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties.
The point that arise for consideration is with regard to quantum.
12. It is not in dispute that the petitioner was met with an accident and sustained injuries.

In order to prove that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle, the petitioner has produced the certified copy of FIR marked as Ex.P1 and also produced certified copy of charge sheet marked as Ex.P4.
Thus, the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.
13. Insofar as quantum of compensation:
It is the case of the petitioner that, petitioner is working as a Lecturer in Government Pre-University College, Sirwar and NC: 2024:KHC-K:3862-DB drawing salary of Rs.40,617/-.
The petitioner has produced the salary certificate which is marked as Ex.P11.

Further, the petitioner in order to establish that she has suffered injuries in the road traffic accident has examined two doctors as PW.3 and PW.4, who have deposed that the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries on her body.

Further, in order to prove that the petitioner has not claimed any medical expenditure incurred by her from the Government and to substantiate the same she has examined the Principal of the Pre-University College, Sirwar, who has deposed that the petitioner is working as a Lecturer and she has not claimed any medical expenditure incurred by her and further deposed that after the accident she has joined the duty and discharging her duties as a Lecturer.

Hence, from the perusal of the evidence, the Tribunal has committed an error in granting compensation under the head loss of future income as the petitioner even after the accident she Jyoti W/O Rajshekar vs The Divisional Coantroller on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139526231/
4 continued to work as a Lecturer in Government Pre-University College, Sirwar.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:3862-DB

Hence, the petitioner is not entitled for compensation under this head loss of future income.
14.
Though the petitioner has produced the medical bills incurred by her and she has not claimed medical expenditure from the Government.

The petitioner has produced Exs.P21, 83, 84, 85 and 86,
the original bills which disclose that the petitioner has paid the amount to the Sparsha Hospital.
The aspect was not considered by the Tribunal and further failed to award compensation under the head medical expenses.
We have perused Exs.P21, 83, 84, 85 and 86 and also the evidence of PW.2, thus Tribunal has committed an error in not granting compensation under the head of medical expenses.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.21,09,680/- under the head of medical expenses.

15. Further, the tribunal has not awarded compensation under the head loss of pain and suffering,
loss of amenities.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:3862-DB compensation of Rs.2,00,000/- under the head pain and suffering,
Rs.50,000/- towards loss of amenities.
16.

Hence, we re-assess the compensation under different heads as under;
Sl.No.
Heads By this Court

1. Injury pain and Rs.2,00,000/-
 sufferings 2. Loss of amenities Rs.50,000/-

3. Medical expenses Rs.21,09,680/-
4. Food, attendant, Rs.50,000/-
 nourishment and  charges 5.

Loss of income during Rs.1,65,552/-
 laid up 6.
Transportation charges Rs.10,000/-
The petitioner is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.25,85,232/- as against Rs.14,27,192/- awarded by the tribunal.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for an enhanced compensation of Rs.11,58,040/- with interest @ 6% p.a.
18.

Hence, we proceed to pass the following:
